reason: H0 exercises only binary parsing through plist_from_bin and immediately frees the result. It does not directly exercise the changed container-mutation APIs, especially their NULL-item contract or mutation-dependent branches such as array replacement/insertion and dictionary replacement, creation, and large-dictionary hash-table initialization.
evidence: H0 calls only plist_from_bin(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data), size, &root_node) and plist_free(root_node).
All four changed public functions add an early `if (!item) { return; }` branch that H0 does not deliberately invoke.
plist_array_set_item has distinct existing-item replacement behavior through plist_array_get_item, plist_free_node, node_insert, and ptr_array_set.
plist_array_insert_item and plist_array_set_item also depend on caller-controlled index `n`, including the `n < INT_MAX` condition.

plist_dict_set_item has separate existing-key and new-key paths and creates a hash table only when `((node_t)node)->count > 500`, requiring constructed mutable state rather than merely parsing and freeing one input.
recommended_action: Add a structure-aware mutation harness that constructs array and dictionary nodes, derives operation sequences, keys, indices, and item values from fuzz input, explicitly calls each affected API with both NULL and non-NULL items, exercises replacement and insertion cases, crosses the dictionary count threshold above 500, and frees all resulting structures.
